errors.quote: The basis vectors $\mathbf b\otimes\mathbf g_j$ of $A\otimes C$ span $B\otimes C$ and the vectors $\mathbf p\otimes\mathbf g_j$ span $P\otimes C$
errors.problem: The vectors $\mathbf g_j$ were introduced as a basis of $G$, not of $C$; here they must be a basis of $C$, which the page never introduces. The argument is right once a basis of $C$ is named.

errors.quote: A form is nondegenerate when its Gram matrix (the matrix of pairings of basis vectors) is invertible, which is why dimensions must be finite.
errors.problem: Nondegeneracy (trivial radical) makes sense in any dimension; the Gram-matrix test is just the finite-dimensional form of it. Finiteness is actually needed for the splitting $A=B\perp P$ and for the dimension counts. The paper simply works in finite-dimensional bilinear spaces ($F=\mathbb Q^h$ or $\mathbb F_2^h$, $\mathcal F=F^{\otimes3}$) and never ties finiteness to the definition.
